title: Uniformizer section and local derived-completeness test
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a scheme $X$. Let $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ and $\underline{\mathcal O_E}\to B$ be the canonical constant-to-completion map [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the global and slice ring sheaves and their standard derived categories of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. For $V\in X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, define $\operatorname{integralCompletionScalarValue}(V)\in B(V)$ to be the value at $V$ of the completed uniformizer section $\pi_X\in\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ [def-sp-completed-uniformizer-section], that is, the image of $\varpi_E$ under the constant-presheaf sheafification unit followed by the canonical constant-to-completion map. For $K\in D(B)$, $U\in X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and a global section $s$ of $B|_U$ on the slice, define $\operatorname{integralCompletionLocalTest}(K,U,s)$ to be $R\mathcal Hom_{B|_U}((B|_U)[1/s][0],K|_U)$. Here the localization is the sheafified sectionwise localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], restriction is the standard derived slice restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction], and internal Hom is the existing derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Scheme and coefficient universes are independent, the site's object and morphism universes are respectively $t+1$ and $t$, and coefficients and modules have size $\max(u,t+1)$. These definitions assert no vanishing or completeness equivalence.
